{"notes": "VISIT 2 (left 2:45). Both tail lines now reach their tips: upper tail to ~(26.7,5.2) and lower tail to ~(27,14.5). The belly line now runs through the crossing and is connected. Doubled-up overlap near (19-22, 11-13) is still there, but those dominoes look connected and aligned. One concern: 3 pale, disconnected dominoes sit just off the line around (23-24, 8.3-9), above the crossing. They are probably the stray one Omar meant to nudge, but I don't know that, and they were still there when I left. If they were bumped they could be a risk to the single run. I don't know who placed which domino, so I rate only on what I saw and heard.

SOFIA: Set the concept and now the plan. At 2:15 she split the work (Hana joins the belly, she does crossing to upper tail) to avoid waiting. At 2:30 she said she was on her last domino at the tip and would inspect the whole tail. She gave a sensible reason for the doubled bit, but asked Jack to check for tilt and gaps. Strong direction and communication. The upper tail is complete, matching her claim. Didn't see her place dominoes. Check that she really does the full-tail inspection and spots the stray dominoes.

OMAR: Earlier gave a clean handoff. At 2:30 he offered to fix an off-side domino and asked Hana to shout if she was already on it, which is good coordination and ownership. Verify it got fixed.

HANA: Silent again this visit. Belly now joins the crossing and the tail is built, so the work seems done. Others talk about her tasks without her replying. Ask whether she's blocked or just quiet, and whether she's heard.

JACK: Deferred on the top line when Sofia claimed it, which was good teamwork. Took on checking the joint before the crossing, and looks to be a quality checker. Didn't see him do it. Check that he checked and noticed the stray dominoes."}
